plan.problem: The post-merge adversarial audit reproduced a bypass where git ls-tree interprets candidate-controlled changed paths as pathspecs, causing 100755 files such as :(literal)docs/payload.md to disappear from executablePaths.
plan.currentContract: collectExecutablePaths calls isExecutableAtRef, which runs git ls-tree <ref> -- <filePath> for each changed path and therefore allows Git pathspec magic to affect executable-mode lookup.
plan.whyExistingIsInsufficient: All Risk/Impact/Verification users share the same executable-path collector, so parity preserves the same wrong answer and a CONTENT/Lite plan can miss the unknown-code floor.
plan.design: Read the complete tree with git ls-tree -r -z, derive an exact literal set of 100755 paths from NUL-delimited records, and compare changed path strings with Set.has rather than passing candidate-controlled names back to Git as pathspecs.
alternativesRejected: Escape only currently known pathspec magic prefixes; future or alternate Git pathspec forms could remain.
Prefix candidate paths with :(literal) while still invoking per-path Git queries; centralized NUL-delimited tree parsing is simpler to reason about and test.
plan.compatibility: Preserve exported isExecutableAtRef/collectExecutablePaths behavior for ordinary paths while making special names literal.
boundaryCases: base-side executable mode is still considered
testPlan: Create a temporary real Git repository with a base commit and executable special-name files in a descendant commit.
Assert collectExecutablePaths returns exact special-name paths.
Assert Lite/CONTENT risk evaluation receives unknown-code and fails.
Assert Impact derives high-risk review/runtime regression requirements from the same executablePaths.
Run Change Operations regression suite and trusted Change PR Gate.
plan.promotionRisk: Staging Change OS only. A regression could misclassify executable paths, so existing trusted gate plus post-fix canary are required.
